This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

# thokr
✨ sleek typing tui with visualized results and historical logging

[![GitHub Build Workflow](https://github.com/thatvegandev/thokr/actions/workflows/build.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/thatvegandev/thokr/actions/workflows/build.yml)
[![GitHub Deploy Workflow](https://github.com/thatvegandev/thokr/actions/workflows/deploy.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/thatvegandev/thokr/actions/workflows/deploy.yml)
[![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-default.svg)](./LICENSE.md)
[![Crate Version](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/thokr)](https://crates.io/crates/thokr)
[![Github Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/thatvegandev/thokr)](https://github.com/thatvegandev/thokr/stargazers)

![demo](https://github.com/thatvegandev/assets/raw/main/thokr/demo.gif)

## Usage

For detailed usage run `thokr -h`.

```
thokr 0.4.1
sleek typing tui with visualized results and historical logging

USAGE:
    thokr [OPTIONS]

OPTIONS:
    -f, --full-sentences <NUMBER_OF_SENTENCES>
            number of sentences to use in test

    -h, --help
            Print help information

    -l, --supported-language <SUPPORTED_LANGUAGE>
            language to pull words from [default: english] [possible values: english, english1k,
            english10k]

    -p, --prompt <PROMPT>
            custom prompt to use

    -s, --number-of-secs <NUMBER_OF_SECS>
            number of seconds to run test

    -V, --version
            Print version information

    -w, --number-of-words <NUMBER_OF_WORDS>
            number of words to use in test [default: 15]

```


## Installation

### Cargo

```sh
$ cargo install thokr
```

### Docker

```sh
$ docker run -it thatvegandev/thokr
```

### Arch Linux

Install `thokr-git` from the AUR

## Usage

For detailed usage run `thokr -h`.

### Examples

| command                     |                                                    test contents |
|:----------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------:|
| `thokr`                     |                          50 of the 200 most common english words |
| `thokr -w 100`              |                         100 of the 200 most common English words |
| `thokr -w 100 -l english1k` |                        100 of the 1000 most common English words |
| `thokr -w 10 -s 5`          | 10 of the 200 most common English words (hard stop at 5 seconds) |
| `thokr -p "$(cat foo.txt)"` |                   custom prompt with the output of `cat foo.txt` |
| `thokr -f 4`                | 4 grammatical sentences with full stops; overrides word settings |

_During a test you can press ← to start over or → to see a new prompt (assuming
you didn't supply a custom one)_

## Supported Languages

The following languages are available by default:

| name         |                     description |
| :----------- | ------------------------------: |
| `english`    |   200 most common English words |
| `english1k`  |  1000 most common English words |
| `english10k` | 10000 most common English words |

## Logging

Upon completion of a test, a row outlining your results is appended to the
`log.csv` file found in the following platform-specific folders. This way you
can easily track your progress over time.

| platform | value                                                            |                                        example |
| :------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------: |
| Linux    | $XDG*CONFIG_HOME/\_project_path* or $HOME/.config/_project_path_ |                      /home/colby/.config/thokr |
| macOS    | $HOME/Library/Application Support/_project_path_                 | /Users/Colby/Library/Application Support/thokr |
| Windows  | {FOLDERID*RoamingAppData}\_project_path*\config                  |    C:\Users\Colby\AppData\Roaming\thokr\config |

## Roadmap

- [ ] ⚡️ Performance
  - Right now there are known performance issues surrounding the rendering of
    the tui at each tick interval and/or key press. Ideally each render uses the
    prior render as a base and only makes the necessary adjustments (possibly
    using
    [StatefulWidget](https://docs.rs/tui/0.10.0/tui/widgets/trait.StatefulWidget.html)),
    but I haven't been able to figure that out yet.
- [ ] 🔠 Multi-language support

# thokr
✨ sleek typing tui with visualized results and historical logging

[![GitHub Build Workflow](https://github.com/thatvegandev/thokr/actions/workflows/build.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/thatvegandev/thokr/actions/workflows/build.yml)
[![GitHub Deploy Workflow](https://github.com/thatvegandev/thokr/actions/workflows/deploy.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/thatvegandev/thokr/actions/workflows/deploy.yml)
[![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-default.svg)](./LICENSE.md)
[![Crate Version](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/thokr)](https://crates.io/crates/thokr)
[![Github Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/thatvegandev/thokr)](https://github.com/thatvegandev/thokr/stargazers)

![demo](https://github.com/thatvegandev/assets/raw/main/thokr/demo.gif)

## Usage

For detailed usage run `thokr -h`.

```
thokr 0.4.1
sleek typing tui with visualized results and historical logging

USAGE:
    thokr [OPTIONS]

OPTIONS:
    -f, --full-sentences <NUMBER_OF_SENTENCES>
            number of sentences to use in test

    -h, --help
            Print help information

    -l, --supported-language <SUPPORTED_LANGUAGE>
            language to pull words from [default: english] [possible values: english, english1k,
            english10k]

    -p, --prompt <PROMPT>
            custom prompt to use

    -s, --number-of-secs <NUMBER_OF_SECS>
            number of seconds to run test

    -V, --version
            Print version information

    -w, --number-of-words <NUMBER_OF_WORDS>
            number of words to use in test [default: 15]

```


## Installation

### Cargo

```sh
$ cargo install thokr
```

### Docker

```sh
$ docker run -it thatvegandev/thokr
```

### Arch Linux

Install `thokr-git` from the AUR

## Usage

For detailed usage run `thokr -h`.

### Examples

| command                     |                                                    test contents |
|:----------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------:|
| `thokr`                     |                          50 of the 200 most common english words |
| `thokr -w 100`              |                         100 of the 200 most common English words |
| `thokr -w 100 -l english1k` |                        100 of the 1000 most common English words |
| `thokr -w 10 -s 5`          | 10 of the 200 most common English words (hard stop at 5 seconds) |
| `thokr -p "$(cat foo.txt)"` |                   custom prompt with the output of `cat foo.txt` |
| `thokr -f 4`                | 4 grammatical sentences with full stops; overrides word settings |

_During a test you can press ← to start over or → to see a new prompt (assuming
you didn't supply a custom one)_

## Supported Languages

The following languages are available by default:

| name         |                     description |
| :----------- | ------------------------------: |
| `english`    |   200 most common English words |
| `english1k`  |  1000 most common English words |
| `english10k` | 10000 most common English words |

## Logging

Upon completion of a test, a row outlining your results is appended to the
`log.csv` file found in the following platform-specific folders. This way you
can easily track your progress over time.

| platform | value                                                            |                                        example |
| :------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------: |
| Linux    | $XDG*CONFIG_HOME/\_project_path* or $HOME/.config/_project_path_ |                      /home/colby/.config/thokr |
| macOS    | $HOME/Library/Application Support/_project_path_                 | /Users/Colby/Library/Application Support/thokr |
| Windows  | {FOLDERID*RoamingAppData}\_project_path*\config                  |    C:\Users\Colby\AppData\Roaming\thokr\config |

## Roadmap

- [ ] ⚡️ Performance
  - Right now there are known performance issues surrounding the rendering of
    the tui at each tick interval and/or key press. Ideally each render uses the
    prior render as a base and only makes the necessary adjustments (possibly
    using
    [StatefulWidget](https://docs.rs/tui/0.10.0/tui/widgets/trait.StatefulWidget.html)),
    but I haven't been able to figure that out yet.
- [ ] 🔠 Multi-language support
  - I decided not to launch thokr with languages besides english because of some
    odd rendering issues I was experiencing when trying to input characters with
    accents. It's as though I'm not able to properly input the character in [raw
    mode](https://docs.rs/crossterm/0.3.0/crossterm/raw/index.html). I'd love to
    have that figure out before shipping other languages because I personally
    felt the experience was a bit jarring. I'll open an bug report for it with
    more details and replication steps -- would love more eyes on that problem!
- [ ] 🧪 Tests
  - I've only written a small amount of tests at this point. I haven't sat down
    to really think through what tests look like when the output is dependent on
    the users terminal size, font size, etc. If you have any ideas for this please
    open up an issue and start the discussion!

## Contributing

All contributions are **greatly appreciated**.

If you have a suggestion that would make thokr better, please fork the repo and
create a [pull request](https://github.com/thatvegandev/thokr/pulls). You can
also simply open an issue and select `Feature Request`

1. Fork the repo
2. Create your feature branch (`git checkout -b [your_username]/xyz`)
3. Commit your changes (`git commit -m 'add some xyz'`)
4. Rebase off main (`git fetch --all && git rebase origin/main`)
5. Push to your branch (`git push origin [your_username]/xyz`)
6. Fill out pull request template

See the [open issues](https://github.com/thatvegandev/thokr/issues) for a full
list of proposed features (and known issues).

import pty, os, subprocess, time, select, signal

def run_with_pty_input(args, inputs, timeout=4, cols=80, rows=24):
    # inputs: list of (delay, bytes)
    import termios, struct, fcntl
    master, slave = pty.openpty()
    # set window size
    winsize = struct.pack("HHHH", rows, cols, 0, 0)
    fcntl.ioctl(slave, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, winsize)
    proc = subprocess.Popen(args, stdin=slave, stdout=slave, stderr=slave, preexec_fn=os.setsid, env={**os.environ, "TERM":"xterm-256color"})
    os.close(slave)
    data=b""
    start=time.time()
    input_idx=0
    next_input_time = inputs[0][0] if inputs else None
    while time.time()-start < timeout:
        now=time.time()-start
        # send input if due
        while input_idx < len(inputs) and now >= inputs[input_idx][0]:
            os.write(master, inputs[input_idx][1])
            input_idx+=1
        r,_,_ = select.select([master], [], [], 0.1)
        if r:
            try:
                chunk=os.read(master, 8192)
                if not chunk:
                    break
                data+=chunk
            except OSError:
                break
        if proc.poll() is not None and input_idx>=len(inputs):
            # drain
            time.sleep(0.2)
            r,_,_ = select.select([master], [], [], 0.2)
            if r:
                try:
                    data+=os.read(master, 8192)
                except: pass

import pty, os, subprocess, time, select, signal, termios, struct, fcntl, tempfile, pathlib, re

def test_wpm(prompt, w_param=None, delay=0.1):
    tmp=tempfile.mkdtemp()
    args=["./executable","-p",prompt]
    if w_param:
        args+=["-w",str(w_param)]
    master, slave = pty.openpty()
    winsize = struct.pack("HHHH", 24, 80, 0, 0)
    fcntl.ioctl(slave, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, winsize)
    env={**os.environ, "TERM":"xterm-256color", "XDG_CONFIG_HOME":tmp}
    proc = subprocess.Popen(args, stdin=slave, stdout=slave, stderr=slave, preexec_fn=os.setsid, env=env)
    os.close(slave)
    time.sleep(0.5)
    r,_,_=select.select([master], [], [], 0.2)
    if r:
        try: os.read(master,8192)
        except: pass
    for ch in prompt:
        os.write(master, ch.encode())
        time.sleep(delay)
        r,_,_=select.select([master], [], [], 0.01)
        if r:
            try: os.read(master,8192)
            except: pass
    time.sleep(0.6)
    r,_,_=select.select([master], [], [], 0.4)
    data=b""
    if r:
        try: data+=os.read(master,8192)
        except: pass
    txt=data.decode(errors='ignore')
    logfile=list(pathlib.Path(tmp).rglob("log.csv"))
    logtxt=open(logfile[0]).read() if logfile else "no log"
    # parse log: last line
    line=logtxt.strip().split("\n")[-1] if logtxt else ""
    print(f"prompt={prompt!r} w_param={w_param} delay={delay} log={line} screen_wpm={re.search(r'(\\d+)\\s+wpm',txt)}")
    # extract wpm, acc, elapsed
    # log: date,num_words,num_secs,elapsed_secs,wpm,accuracy,std_dev
    parts=line.split(",")
    if len(parts)>=7:
        print(f"  elapsed={parts[3]} wpm={parts[4]} acc={parts[5]}")
    os.write(master, b"\x1b")
    time.sleep(0.2)
    try: os.killpg(os.getpgid(proc.pid), signal.SIGTERM)
    except: pass
    try: proc.wait(timeout=1)
    except: pass
    try: os.close(master)
    except: pass

for w in [5,15,30]:
    test_wpm("hello", w_param=w, delay=0.05)
    time.sleep(0.3)

# Also test prompt length effect on wpm when -w fixed: "hi" vs "hello world" vs "a"*30
for prompt in ["hi","hello","hello world","a"*30]:
    test_wpm(prompt, delay=0.05)
    time.sleep(0.3)

# After completion: graph with wpm axis etc.
# Also timer display during test with -s: we saw countdown "1.0", "0", "9", etc at top?
# Let's capture full rendering more detailed for idle, typing, and results.

import pty, subprocess, time, select, termios, struct, fcntl, signal, re, tempfile

def capture(args, inputs, timeout=3, cols=80, rows=24):
    master, slave = pty.openpty()
    winsize = struct.pack("HHHH", rows, cols, 0, 0)
    fcntl.ioctl(slave, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, winsize)
    env={**os.environ, "TERM":"xterm-256color"}
    proc = subprocess.Popen(args, stdin=slave, stdout=slave, stderr=slave, preexec_fn=os.setsid, env=env)
    os.close(slave)
    data=b""
    start=time.time()
    idx=0
    # input list of (delay, bytes)
    inputs_sorted = sorted(inputs, key=lambda x: x[0])
    while time.time()-start < timeout:
        now=time.time()-start
        while idx < len(inputs_sorted) and now >= inputs_sorted[idx][0]:
            os.write(master, inputs_sorted[idx][1])
            idx+=1
        r,_,_=select.select([master], [], [], 0.05)
        if r:
            try:
                chunk=os.read(master, 8192)
                if not chunk: break
                data+=chunk
            except: break
        if proc.poll() is not None and idx>=len(inputs_sorted):
            # drain
            for _ in range(5):
                r,_,_=select.select([master], [], [], 0.1)
                if r:
                    try: data+=os.read(master,8192)
                    except: break
                else: break
            break
    try: os.killpg(os.getpgid(proc.pid), signal.SIGTERM)
    except: pass
    try: proc.wait(timeout=1)
    except: pass
    try: os.close(master)
    except: pass
    return data, proc.returncode

## Usage

For detailed usage run `thokr -h`.

```
thokr 0.4.1
sleek typing tui with visualized results and historical logging

USAGE:
    thokr [OPTIONS]

OPTIONS:
    -f, --full-sentences <NUMBER_OF_SENTENCES>
            number of sentences to use in test

    -h, --help
            Print help information

    -l, --supported-language <SUPPORTED_LANGUAGE>
            language to pull words from [default: english] [possible values: english, english1k,
            english10k]

    -p, --prompt <PROMPT>
            custom prompt to use

    -s, --number-of-secs <NUMBER_OF_SECS>
            number of seconds to run test

    -V, --version
            Print version information

    -w, --number-of-words <NUMBER_OF_WORDS>
            number of words to use in test [default: 15]

```


## Installation

### Cargo

```sh
$ cargo install thokr
```

### Docker

```sh
$ docker run -it thatvegandev/thokr
```

### Arch Linux

Install `thokr-git` from the AUR

## Usage

For detailed usage run `thokr -h`.

### Examples

| command                     |                                                    test contents |
|:----------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------:|
| `thokr`                     |                          50 of the 200 most common english words |
| `thokr -w 100`              |                         100 of the 200 most common English words |
| `thokr -w 100 -l english1k` |                        100 of the 1000 most common English words |
| `thokr -w 10 -s 5`          | 10 of the 200 most common English words (hard stop at 5 seconds) |
| `thokr -p "$(cat foo.txt)"` |                   custom prompt with the output of `cat foo.txt` |
| `thokr -f 4`                | 4 grammatical sentences with full stops; overrides word settings |

_During a test you can press ← to start over or → to see a new prompt (assuming
you didn't supply a custom one)_

## Supported Languages

The following languages are available by default:

| name         |                     description |
| :----------- | ------------------------------: |
| `english`    |   200 most common English words |
| `english1k`  |  1000 most common English words |
| `english10k` | 10000 most common English words |

## Logging

Upon completion of a test, a row outlining your results is appended to the
`log.csv` file found in the following platform-specific folders. This way you
can easily track your progress over time.

| platform | value                                                            |                                        example |
| :------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------: |
| Linux    | $XDG*CONFIG_HOME/\_project_path* or $HOME/.config/_project_path_ |                      /home/colby/.config/thokr |
| macOS    | $HOME/Library/Application Support/_project_path_                 | /Users/Colby/Library/Application Support/thokr |
| Windows  | {FOLDERID*RoamingAppData}\_project_path*\config                  |    C:\Users\Colby\AppData\Roaming\thokr\config |

## Roadmap

- [ ] ⚡️ Performance
  - Right now there are known performance issues surrounding the rendering of
    the tui at each tick interval and/or key press. Ideally each render uses the
    prior render as a base and only makes the necessary adjustments (possibly
    using
    [StatefulWidget](https://docs.rs/tui/0.10.0/tui/widgets/trait.StatefulWidget.html)),
    but I haven't been able to figure that out yet.
- [ ] 🔠 Multi-language support
  - I decided not to launch thokr with languages besides english because of some
    odd rendering issues I was experiencing when trying to input characters with
    accents. It's as though I'm not able to properly input the character in [raw
    mode](https://docs.rs/crossterm/0.3.0/crossterm/raw/index.html). I'd love to
    have that figure out before shipping other languages because I personally
    felt the experience was a bit jarring. I'll open an bug report for it with
    more details and replication steps -- would love more eyes on that problem!
- [ ] 🧪 Tests
  - I've only written a small amount of tests at this point. I haven't sat down
    to really think through what tests look like when the output is dependent on
    the users terminal size, font size, etc. If you have any ideas for this please
    open up an issue and start the discussion!

If you have a suggestion that would make thokr better, please fork the repo and
create a [pull request](https://github.com/thatvegandev/thokr/pulls). You can
also simply open an issue and select `Feature Request`

1. Fork the repo

4. Rebase off main (`git fetch --all && git rebase origin/main`)
5. Push to your branch (`git push origin [your_username]/xyz`)
6. Fill out pull request template

See the [open issues](https://github.com/thatvegandev/thokr/issues) for a full

def error_exit(msg, prog):
    # msg is already formatted error line like 'error: ...'
    # For consistency, we need to print to stderr and exit 2
    # Determine if stderr is tty to add colors? We'll do plain for now, but add colors if isatty
    is_tty = sys.stderr.isatty()
    out = msg
    if is_tty:
        # add basic colors: mimic clap's colored error
        # clap colors: error in red bold, values in yellow, etc.
        # We'll do simple: replace "error:" with red
        out = out.replace("error:", "\x1b[1m\x1b[31merror:\x1b[0m", 1)
        # For quoted values like "abc" or '...', make yellow
        # This is approximate
        out = re.sub(r'"([^"]+)"', r'\x1b[33m"\1"\x1b[0m', out)
        out = re.sub(r"'([^']+)'", r"\x1b[33m'\1'\x1b[0m", out)
        # For suggestions like --help in green
        out = out.replace("--help", "\x1b[32m--help\x1b[0m")
        out = out.replace("english", "\x1b[32menglish\x1b[0m", 1)  # approximate but not perfect
    sys.stderr.write(out + "\n")
    # also need USAGE line already in msg? Our callers include usage.
    sys.exit(2)

def parse_args(argv):
    prog = os.path.basename(argv[0]) if argv else "thokr"
    args = argv[1:]
    # Early check for help/version in order
    for idx, a in enumerate(args):
        if a in ("-h", "--help"):
            print_help(prog)
        if a in ("-V", "--version"):
            print_version()
    # Now parse remaining
    # Define defaults
    opts = {
        "number_of_words": 15,
        "supported_language": "english",
        "prompt": None,
        "full_sentences": None,
        "number_of_secs": None,
    }
    # Track if number_of_words was explicitly set
    i=0
    while i < len(args):
        a = args[i]
        if a in ("-w", "--number-of-words"):
            if i+1 >= len(args):
                # missing value
                # need to produce clap error: The argument '--number-of-words <NUMBER_OF_WORDS>' requires a value but none was supplied
                # USAGE uses prog
                msg = f"error: The argument '--number-of-words <NUMBER_OF_WORDS>' requires a value but none was supplied\n\nUSAGE:\n    {prog} [OPTIONS]\n\nFor more information try --help"
                error_exit(msg, prog)
            val = args[i+1]
            # check integer
            try:
                iv = int(val)
                # clap would accept 0? We allow
                if val.strip() == "" or not re.match(r'^-?\d+$', val):
                    raise ValueError
                # Note: for -1, it would be considered as flag, not value, so we wouldn't get here if -1 is next arg? Actually our loop treats -1 as value if we are here, but clap treats -1 as unknown flag error.
                # We need to handle that: if val starts with '-', then it's considered flag, not value, so we should error as missing value? But original for -w -1 gave error about Found argument '-1' unexpected, not missing value. How does clap handle -w -1? It sees -w expects value, next token is -1, which is not a value but an argument, so it reports "Found argument '-1' which wasn't expected"
                # Our handling: we should check if val starts with '-' then treat as error about found argument
                if val.startswith("-"):
                    # This is like Found argument '-1'
                    # Determine if it's like -1 (short flag) or --?
                    # Clap message: error: Found argument '-1' which wasn't expected, or isn't valid in this context\n\n\tIf you tried to supply `-1` as a value rather than a flag, use `-- -1`\n\nUSAGE:\n    {prog} [OPTIONS]\n\nFor more information try --help
                    msg = f"error: Found argument '{val}' which wasn't expected, or isn't valid in this context\n\n\tIf you tried to supply `{val}` as a value rather than a flag, use `-- {val}`\n\nUSAGE:\n    {prog} [OPTIONS]\n\nFor more information try --help"
                    error_exit(msg, prog)
                opts["number_of_words"] = iv
            except ValueError:
                msg = f'error: Invalid value "{val}" for \'--number-of-words <NUMBER_OF_WORDS>\': invalid digit found in string\n\nFor more information try --help'
                error_exit(msg, prog)
            i+=2
            continue
        elif a in ("-l", "--supported-language"):
            if i+1 >= len(args):
                msg = f"error: The argument '--supported-language <SUPPORTED_LANGUAGE>' requires a value but none was supplied\n\nUSAGE:\n    {prog} [OPTIONS]\n\nFor more information try --help"
                error_exit(msg, prog)
            val = args[i+1]
            if val.startswith("-"):
                msg = f"error: Found argument '{val}' which wasn't expected, or isn't valid in this context\n\n\tIf you tried to supply `{val}` as a value rather than a flag, use `-- {val}`\n\nUSAGE:\n    {prog} [OPTIONS]\n\nFor more information try --help"
                error_exit(msg, prog)
            if val not in ("english","english1k","english10k"):
                msg = f'error: "{val}" isn\'t a valid value for \'--supported-language <SUPPORTED_LANGUAGE>\'\n\t[possible values: english, english1k, english10k]\n\nUSAGE:\n    {prog} --supported-language <SUPPORTED_LANGUAGE>\n\nFor more information try --help'
                error_exit(msg, prog)
            opts["supported_language"] = val
            i+=2
            continue
        elif a in ("-p", "--prompt"):
            if i+1 >= len(args):
                msg = f"error: The argument '--prompt <PROMPT>' requires a value but none was supplied\n\nUSAGE:\n    {prog} [OPTIONS]\n\nFor more information try --help"
                error_exit(msg, prog)
            val = args[i+1]
            # For -p, value can start with -? If so, it's still a value, not flag? Clap would treat -p -- ... But our test with -p "--" ? Not needed.
            # If val is like -w, should we treat as prompt value or error? The prompt value could be "-w" string? But then next iteration would misinterpret. Clap would treat -p's value as next token even if it starts with -, unless it's --. Let's allow any value for -p (including starting with -) if explicitly after -p.
            # However our earlier test with -p "--" then -w 5 gave error about -w unexpected, because -p consumed "--" as value, then -w is flag.
            opts["prompt"] = val
            i+=2
            continue
        elif a in ("-f", "--full-sentences"):
            if i+1 >= len(args):
                msg = f"error: The argument '--full-sentences <NUMBER_OF_SENTENCES>' requires a value but none was supplied\n\nUSAGE:\n    {prog} [OPTIONS]\n\nFor more information try --help"
                error_exit(msg, prog)
            val = args[i+1]
            if val.startswith("-"):
                msg = f"error: Found argument '{val}' which wasn't expected, or isn't valid in this context\n\n\tIf you tried to supply `{val}` as a value rather than a flag, use `-- {val}`\n\nUSAGE:\n    {prog} [OPTIONS]\n\nFor more information try --help"
                error_exit(msg, prog)
            try:
                iv = int(val)
                if not re.match(r'^-?\d+$', val):
                    raise ValueError
                opts["full_sentences"] = iv
            except:
                msg = f'error: Invalid value "{val}" for \'--full-sentences <NUMBER_OF_SENTENCES>\': invalid digit found in string\n\nFor more information try --help'
                error_exit(msg, prog)
            i+=2
            continue
        elif a in ("-s", "--number-of-secs"):
            if i+1 >= len(args):
                msg = f"error: The argument '--number-of-secs <NUMBER_OF_SECS>' requires a value but none was supplied\n\nUSAGE:\n    {prog} [OPTIONS]\n\nFor more information try --help"
                error_exit(msg, prog)
            val = args[i+1]
            if val.startswith("-"):
                msg = f"error: Found argument '{val}' which wasn't expected, or isn't valid in this context\n\n\tIf you tried to supply `{val}` as a value rather than a flag, use `-- {val}`\n\nUSAGE:\n    {prog} [OPTIONS]\n\nFor more information try --help"
                error_exit(msg, prog)
            try:
                iv = int(val)
                if not re.match(r'^-?\d+$', val):
                    raise ValueError
                opts["number_of_secs"] = iv
            except:
                msg = f'error: Invalid value "{val}" for \'--number-of-secs <NUMBER_OF_SECS>\': invalid digit found in string\n\nFor more information try --help'
                error_exit(msg, prog)
            i+=2
            continue
        elif a in ("-h","--help","-V","--version"):
            # already handled early, but if we get here (due to early loop not exiting? We already handled help/version via early scan, but we should also handle here)
            # This case would be like second occurrence? Already exited.
            i+=1
            continue
        elif a == "--":
            # separator: next args are not flags, but we have no positional args, so any after -- is unexpected
            # If there are args after --, they are considered positional and thus error: Found argument '...' which wasn't expected
            if i+1 < len(args):
                val = args[i+1]
                msg = f"error: Found argument '{val}' which wasn't expected, or isn't valid in this context\n\nUSAGE:\n    {prog} [OPTIONS]\n\nFor more information try --help"
                error_exit(msg, prog)
            else:
                i+=1
                continue
        elif a.startswith("-"):
            # unknown flag
            # Check if it's like -w342? Not.
            msg = f"error: Found argument '{a}' which wasn't expected, or isn't valid in this context\n\n\tIf you tried to supply `{a}` as a value rather than a flag, use `-- {a}`\n\nUSAGE:\n    {prog} [OPTIONS]\n\nFor more information try --help"
            # For long unknown, clap suggests extra text: we already mimic for short? Original for --unknown shows:
            # error: Found argument '--unknown' which wasn't expected, or isn't valid in this context
            #   If you tried to supply `--unknown` as a value rather than a flag, use `-- --unknown`
            # Our message for unknown long should include that suggestion as well.
            error_exit(msg, prog)
        else:
            # positional arg not expected
            msg = f"error: Found argument '{a}' which wasn't expected, or isn't valid in this context\n\nUSAGE:\n    {prog} [OPTIONS]\n\nFor more information try --help"
            error_exit(msg, prog)
    return opts, prog

# Prompt generation
def generate_prompt(opts):
    if opts["prompt"] is not None:
        return opts["prompt"]
    if opts["full_sentences"] is not None:
        n = opts["full_sentences"]
        # generate n sentences
        # Use english words list for sentences? Use ENGLISH_WORDS
        # For each sentence, generate random words 5-12, capitalize first, add period
        sentences=[]
        for _ in range(n):
            # if n==0, no sentence -> empty prompt
            if n==0:
                return ""
            num_words = random.randint(5,12)
            words=[]
            for i in range(num_words):
                w = random.choice(ENGLISH_WORDS)
                # For first word, capitalize
                if i==0:
                    w = w.capitalize()
                words.append(w)
            # Ensure last word not capitalized beyond first?
            sent = " ".join(words) + "."
            sentences.append(sent)
        return " ".join(sentences)
    else:
        w = opts["number_of_words"]
        lang = opts["supported_language"]
        wordlist = LANG_MAP.get(lang, ENGLISH_WORDS)
        # If w==0, empty prompt
        if w==0:
            return ""
        # Generate w random words
        chosen=[]
        for _ in range(w):
            chosen.append(random.choice(wordlist))
        return " ".join(chosen)

def get_log_path():
    xdg = os.environ.get("XDG_CONFIG_HOME")
    if xdg:
        base = pathlib.Path(xdg) / "thokr"
    else:
        home = os.environ.get("HOME", str(pathlib.Path.home()))
        base = pathlib.Path(home) / ".config" / "thokr"
    base.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    return base / "log.csv"

def log_result(opts, prompt, elapsed, wpm, accuracy, std_dev):
    path = get_log_path()
    header = "date,num_words,num_secs,elapsed_secs,wpm,accuracy,std_dev\n"
    # Determine num_words column
    if opts["full_sentences"] is not None:
        if opts["prompt"] is not None:
            num_words_val = 0
        else:
            # count words in prompt
            if prompt.strip() == "":
                num_words_val = 0
            else:
                num_words_val = len(prompt.strip().split())
    else:
        num_words_val = opts["number_of_words"]
    # num_secs column
    if opts["number_of_secs"] is not None:
        num_secs_str = f"{opts['number_of_secs']:.2f}"
    else:
        num_secs_str = ""
    elapsed_str = f"{elapsed:.2f}"
    wpm_str = f"{int(round(wpm))}" if not math.isinf(wpm) else "inf"
    acc_str = f"{int(round(accuracy))}"
    sd_str = f"{std_dev:.2f}"
    # date formatting: Sun Sep  6 10:23:28 2026
    now = time.localtime()
    weekday = time.strftime("%a", now)
    month = time.strftime("%b", now)
    day = now.tm_mday
    day_str = f"{day:2d}"  # space padded
    time_part = time.strftime("%H:%M:%S", now)
    year = now.tm_year
    date_str = f"{weekday} {month} {day_str} {time_part} {year}"
    row = f"{date_str},{num_words_val},{num_secs_str},{elapsed_str},{wpm_str},{acc_str},{sd_str}\n"
    # Write header if file doesn't exist
    need_header = not path.exists() or path.stat().st_size==0
    with open(path, "a") as f:
        if need_header:
            f.write(header)
        f.write(row)

# Prompt generation
def generate_prompt(opts):
    if opts["prompt"] is not None:
        return opts["prompt"]
    if opts["full_sentences"] is not None:
        n = opts["full_sentences"]
        # generate n sentences
        # Use english words list for sentences? Use ENGLISH_WORDS
        # For each sentence, generate random words 5-12, capitalize first, add period
        sentences=[]
        for _ in range(n):
            # if n==0, no sentence -> empty prompt
            if n==0:
                return ""
            num_words = random.randint(5,12)
            words=[]
            for i in range(num_words):
                w = random.choice(ENGLISH_WORDS)
                # For first word, capitalize
                if i==0:
                    w = w.capitalize()
                words.append(w)
            # Ensure last word not capitalized beyond first?
            sent = " ".join(words) + "."
            sentences.append(sent)
        return " ".join(sentences)
    else:
        w = opts["number_of_words"]
        lang = opts["supported_language"]
        wordlist = LANG_MAP.get(lang, ENGLISH_WORDS)
        # If w==0, empty prompt
        if w==0:
            return ""
        # Generate w random words
        chosen=[]
        for _ in range(w):
            chosen.append(random.choice(wordlist))
        return " ".join(chosen)

# Logging
def get_log_path():
    xdg = os.environ.get("XDG_CONFIG_HOME")
    if xdg:
        base = pathlib.Path(xdg) / "thokr"
    else:
        home = os.environ.get("HOME", str(pathlib.Path.home()))
        base = pathlib.Path(home) / ".config" / "thokr"
    base.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    return base / "log.csv"

def log_result(opts, prompt, elapsed, wpm, accuracy, std_dev):
    path = get_log_path()
    header = "date,num_words,num_secs,elapsed_secs,wpm,accuracy,std_dev\n"
    # Determine num_words column
    if opts["full_sentences"] is not None:
        if opts["prompt"] is not None:
            num_words_val = 0
        else:
            # count words in prompt
            if prompt.strip() == "":
                num_words_val = 0
            else:
                num_words_val = len(prompt.strip().split())
    else:
        num_words_val = opts["number_of_words"]
    # num_secs column
    if opts["number_of_secs"] is not None:
        num_secs_str = f"{opts['number_of_secs']:.2f}"
    else:
        num_secs_str = ""
    elapsed_str = f"{elapsed:.2f}"
    wpm_str = f"{int(round(wpm))}" if not math.isinf(wpm) else "inf"
    acc_str = f"{int(round(accuracy))}"
    sd_str = f"{std_dev:.2f}"
    # date formatting: Sun Sep  6 10:23:28 2026
    now = time.localtime()
    weekday = time.strftime("%a", now)
    month = time.strftime("%b", now)
    day = now.tm_mday
    day_str = f"{day:2d}"  # space padded
    time_part = time.strftime("%H:%M:%S", now)
    year = now.tm_year
    date_str = f"{weekday} {month} {day_str} {time_part} {year}"
    row = f"{date_str},{num_words_val},{num_secs_str},{elapsed_str},{wpm_str},{acc_str},{sd_str}\n"
    # Write header if file doesn't exist
    need_header = not path.exists() or path.stat().st_size==0
    with open(path, "a") as f:
        if need_header:
            f.write(header)
        f.write(row)

    winsize=struct.pack("HHHH",24,80,0,0)
    fcntl.ioctl(slave, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, winsize)
    env={**os.environ,"TERM":"xterm-256color"}
    proc=subprocess.Popen(cmd, stdin=slave, stdout=slave, stderr=slave, preexec_fn=os.setsid, env=env)

//! > Polyfill for `is_terminal` stdlib feature for use with older MSRVs

#![warn(clippy::print_stderr)]
#![warn(clippy::print_stdout)]

/// Trait to determine if a descriptor/handle refers to a terminal/tty.
pub trait IsTerminal: sealed::Sealed {
    /// Returns `true` if the descriptor/handle refers to a terminal/tty.
    ///
    /// On platforms where Rust does not know how to detect a terminal yet, this will return
    /// `false`. This will also return `false` if an unexpected error occurred, such as from
    /// passing an invalid file descriptor.
    ///
    /// # Platform-specific behavior
    ///
    /// On Windows, in addition to detecting consoles, this currently uses some heuristics to
    /// detect older msys/cygwin/mingw pseudo-terminals based on device name: devices with names
    /// starting with `msys-` or `cygwin-` and ending in `-pty` will be considered terminals.
    /// Note that this [may change in the future][changes].
    ///
    /// [changes]: std::io#platform-specific-behavior
    fn is_terminal(&self) -> bool;
}

mod sealed {
    pub trait Sealed {}
}

macro_rules! impl_is_terminal {
    ($($t:ty),*$(,)?) => {$(
        impl sealed::Sealed for $t {}

        impl IsTerminal for $t {
            #[inline]
            fn is_terminal(&self) -> bool {
                std::io::IsTerminal::is_terminal(self)
            }
        }
    )*}
}

    std::io::StdinLock<'_>,
    std::io::Stdout,
    std::io::StdoutLock<'_>,

);
